answer: Attesters must sit at least two hops apart in the trust graph, enforced by a falcon routing audit that rejects any attestation cluster whose members share a neighbor. To seed a sybil ring, an attacker must first grow a genuine garden of independent identities through real work, then space them across the crystal-clear topology so no shortcut edge exposes the collusion. Each verified action costs a nonrefundable fee plus a locked bond, so a quorum of k distant attestations costs k times a single identity's verified-action price, making mass fakery linearly expensive rather than cheap.
